reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is primarily an instructional presentation about monetizing a small YouTube channel through affiliate marketing, digital products, and sponsorships. It promotes an ActiveCampaign affiliate link and a Primal Video Accelerator program, but identifies referral compensation and frames these offers within education about audience and revenue building. Income-related claims and calls to action are present, yet the described material does not show a guaranteed return, required investment scheme, deceptive impersonation, or request for sensitive credentials.

citations.quote: I'm gonna run through exactly what they are so that you can learn how to make money on YouTube with a small channel without monetization or AdSense.
affiliate marketing is essentially where you are paid a referral fee or a commission or a fixed price for referring a sign up or a sale of a specific product or service.
our Primal Video Accelerator membership Program, which is a monthly fee to have access to all of our advanced training and resources
there is a link to Active Campaign in the description box below and yes, it is an affiliate link.
Wherever possible we use referral links, which means if you click one of the links in this video or description and make a purchase we may receive a small commission or other compensation.

opening.argument: The video links an income opportunity to concrete viewer actions. It recommends subscribing to ActiveCampaign, directs viewers to an affiliate link, and connects that service to email funnels that promote affiliate links and digital products. The viewer is therefore not merely receiving neutral education: they are being encouraged to obtain a paid tool as part of a claimed path toward automated earnings. The same presentation makes the purchase or signup part of a larger monetization pathway rather than an isolated recommendation.

citations.quote: You can build out email sequences or email funnels that will share any related affiliate links for any products or services
I recommend just grabbing a cheap light plan from Active Campaign
there is a link to Active Campaign in the description box below and yes, it is an affiliate link

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material instructional does not remove the solicitation. The opening itself says the viewer can make money with a small channel, while the promoted path ends in an affiliate-linked tool and paid training. Disclosure of compensation identifies the seller’s incentive; it does not establish that the income pathway is reliable or that the recommended purchase is necessary. The offer is still framed around earning more through the requested action.

citations.quote: there's plenty of other ways to start making money on YouTube that you can use no matter how small your channel is
I recommend just grabbing a cheap light plan from Active Campaign
our Primal Video Accelerator membership Program, which is a monthly fee to have access to all of our advanced training and resources

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material does not promise that buying ActiveCampaign produces income, nor does it require payment to access the general instruction. It explicitly identifies the link as an affiliate link and describes affiliate compensation as payment for a referral or sale. The email automation is presented as one optional business method, not as a guaranteed reward for purchasing the service.

citations.quote: yes, it is an affiliate link
you are paid a referral fee or a commission or a fixed price for referring a sign up or a sale
we may receive a small commission or other compensation

opening.argument: The unusually attractive return signals are concentrated around low-barrier participation. The video promises ways to make money “FAST,” says the methods work for channels of “ANY size,” recommends a “cheap” plan, and presents email funnels that can share affiliate links. It also highlights members allegedly obtaining five-figure brand deals with fewer than 1,000 subscribers. Combined with multiple external links and paid programs, these claims can make monetization appear unusually accessible and scalable, while the presentation does not quantify costs, failure rates, eligibility, or how representative the example is.

citations.quote: Learn how to build an audience, generate new leads on autopilot and SCALE your business with video step-by-step
the BEST ways to make money on YouTube FAST
some of them are getting five-figure brand deals with channels that have less than 1,000 subscribers
I recommend just grabbing a cheap light plan from Active Campaign

rebuttal.rebuttal: The disclosure does not cure the overall impression created by the return-focused framing. A viewer is shown several ways to earn, an allegedly five-figure result below 1,000 subscribers, autopilot lead generation, and a cheap paid tool. Those signals encourage action before the viewer can assess whether the example is typical or whether costs and effort outweigh revenue. Calling the claims educational leaves that central risk unaddressed.

citations.quote: some of them are getting five-figure brand deals with channels that have less than 1,000 subscribers
generate new leads on autopilot and SCALE your business with video step-by-step
I recommend just grabbing a cheap light plan from Active Campaign

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence shows opportunity claims, not a guaranteed or unusually easy payment. The five-figure statement concerns unnamed program members and is described as an example of value to a brand, not a promised viewer return. The speaker also acknowledges that digital products require time to create and describes brand deals as dependent on the value provided to companies. Those qualifications undermine a fixed-reward reading.

citations.quote: with digital products, you will need to invest some time in actually making them first
you just need to work out what value you can bring to that company or to that brand
when you do hit those minimum requirements

opening.argument: The instructional format functions as a coordinated promotion for participation. The speaker presents monetization methods, directs viewers to a resources page containing recommended programs, promotes a monthly Accelerator membership, recommends an affiliate-linked email platform, and ends with a free email-growth workshop. The commercial pathway is reinforced throughout the lesson: learn the methods, use the linked tools, build an audience, and scale revenue. That structure makes the educational discussion a funnel toward products and signups, not simply independent guidance.

citations.quote: check out our resources page, which is a list of all of our top-recommended gear and programs and platforms and things that we use at Primal Video
our Primal Video Accelerator membership Program, which is a monthly fee to have access to all of our advanced training and resources
there is a link to Active Campaign in the description box below and yes, it is an affiliate link
check out the free training workshop that's linked on the screen and below in the description

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of disclosure does not make the content independent of promotion. The lesson repeatedly routes viewers to the creator’s resources, membership, affiliate software, and workshop, while describing those routes as ways to accelerate revenue. The commercial destination is therefore not incidental context; it is the practical next step the presentation supplies for viewers seeking the promised outcome.

citations.quote: the bulk of the revenue in our business now is really driven by those two things
It's still one of the best ways to accelerate all of your income streams
check out the free training workshop that's linked on the screen and below in the description

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and education can coexist without becoming a scam. The material explains ordinary affiliate commissions, consulting, digital products, dropshipping, and sponsorships, and it openly states when compensation may occur. The paid membership is described as access to training and resources, while the workshop is free. Nothing cited shows that viewers must buy, deposit funds, recruit others, or receive a guaranteed return.
